inputs.fetch_note: Read by the pack author at the pinned commit (the v0.23.0 release tag). The task loads its dataset through utils.py (a snapshot download of ai-safety-institute/AgentHarm at the AGENTHARM_DATASET_REVISION pin in that file), not an hf_dataset call; the FieldSpec record mapping, the default agent's prompt composition (prompts.py, agents/default_agent.py), and the combined scorer's two model judges with their task-arg defaults (scorer.py, benchmark/grading_utils.py) are all encoded in the builder script. Machine-verifiable link is the builder script content hash; this pin is for human audit of those constants.

First 12 rows of the test_public split (config 'harmful') via the HuggingFace datasets-server rows API. The hash covers exactly the 12 row payloads consumed (r['row'] per row), as a JSON array in canonical form (keys sorted, compact separators, UTF-8). The task reads the same records from benchmark/harmful_behaviors_test_public.json in the dataset repo snapshot pinned at e23b3fe60a0da9037314b88e5ee3a0c054970dad; the author verified the rows are field-for-field identical to that file and that the dataset repo HEAD currently equals the pinned revision. Any upstream change fails this hash loudly.

The translation script for this pack, versioned in this repository (builders/build_agentharm_card.py) alongside the pack, so pack and builder land in one commit; earlier packs pin builders in the evalwarden repo instead. The verifier fetches it from this repository's main branch and verifies it byte-for-byte: the content hash is the pin, and any drift fails loudly. The verifier imports it and runs build_agentharm only.

translation.notes: The grader is hybrid: per-behavior grading functions mix deterministic transcript checks with semantic-judge pass/fail calls, and a refusal judge classifies every assistant message. evalwarden's grader record is singular, so the pack models the grader by its model-graded components (kind 'judge'), per the MATH pack's precedent that a definition is modeled by its most integrity-relevant component, and the audit's JUDGE-001 findings attach to those components. The user message is the composed 'empty' template over the record's prompt: a blank line, then the prompt verbatim.

findings.title: Model judge has no labeled calibration set
findings.message: A model judge with no labeled calibration set is an unvalidated measurement instrument: its scores have no demonstrated relationship to human judgment. Unanchored rubrics and unpinned sampling temperature make the verdicts drift further without anyone noticing.
evidence: grader uses model judge openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (task defaults for both the refusal judge and the semantic judge; overridable via the task's refusal_judge / semantic_judge arguments) with no reference labels attached.
Judge scores are unvalidated against human judgment.
findings.remediation: Collect a labeled calibration set and report judge-vs-human agreement before trusting scores; anchor the rubric scale with explicit examples per level; pin temperature to 0 or take multiple repeats per item.

findings.title: Judge rubric has no explicit scale anchors
findings.message: A model judge with no labeled calibration set is an unvalidated measurement instrument: its scores have no demonstrated relationship to human judgment. Unanchored rubrics and unpinned sampling temperature make the verdicts drift further without anyone noticing.
evidence: judge rubric defines criteria but no anchored scale levels.
Without anchors, score meanings drift between runs and reviewers.
findings.remediation: Collect a labeled calibration set and report judge-vs-human agreement before trusting scores; anchor the rubric scale with explicit examples per level; pin temperature to 0 or take multiple repeats per item.

runs_coverage_note: Definition-level card: no run records exist. Without runs, COST-002..004 and the attempt leg of GRAD-002 cannot fire; without judgments, trajectories, or repeated-run scores, JUDGE-003..009, TRAJ-001..002, NOISE-001..002, and DATA-001..003 stay silent, and GRAD-003 has no declared verifier rule or cached outputs to re-score. JUDGE-001 fires on the definition alone (it needs only the grader record); JUDGE-002 does not apply to the pointwise refusal and semantic judgments. A definition-level card is a floor, not a ceiling.

canonicalization.applies_to: the generated card HTML, before sha256
canonicalization.rule: Two mechanical substitutions: (1) replace <footer>...</footer> with <footer></footer>; (2) replace the methodology-table Generated row timestamp cell with the literal TIMESTAMP. The harness version string is kept: the pack pins the exact version, so a version mismatch must fail, not be normalized away.

repro.command: Save the pack as evidence-pack.json, then run: curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jurayh/evidence-registry/b7d79a06abca949a3abc3ea6dfa51f004e4e6f7f/verify_pack.py -o /tmp/ep_verify.py && python3 /tmp/ep_verify.py evidence-pack.json --work-dir /tmp/ep_work
